Parse and execute a known command without sending it to the model. A resolved command's lifecycle is logged: `command/run` is appended before the handler is invoked and `command/done` after settlement (a thrown or aborted handler settles as `kind: 'error'`). Both are direct log-only appends — no turn wraps them, and persistence drains them at ordinary checkpoints. Admission misses (syntax or unknown name) log nothing — they never entered a handler. A `command/run` append failure fails the execution loud; a `command/done` append failure on the handler-failure path is contained so the handler's own error stays the reported failure. Attachment admission is enforced here, not in the composer: attachments sent to a command that does not declare `input.attachments`, an absent attachment store, and an exceeded image limit each settle as an error result before the handler runs. Validation rejection starts no attachment writes; a storage failure can leave only unreachable content-addressed objects for deferred collection.
